report.source_text: After discussions between the interventional radiologist, general surgeon and haematologist, a conservative approach to management was taken. The patient’s old age, moderate frailty and comorbidities favoured conservative treatment, with an interventional approach to be considered if conservative measures were unsuccessful. A total of 6 units of packed red blood cells were transfused over the course of 5 days. Tranexamic acid was also administered during the same time period at a regime of 1 g three times a day. Empirical antibiotic cover was also given. As there was no coagulopathy and a significant interval since the last enoxaparin injection, no reversal agent nor coagulation factors were given. After monitoring for 5 days, the patient’s haemoglobin normalized to 121 g/l. She was subsequently discharged following 5 further days. No routine follow-up was required.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 79-year-old woman with neurofibromatosis type-1 (NF1) was admitted 1 week prior with COVID-19 pneumonitis and placed on high-dose subcutaneous enoxaparin prophylaxis (1 mg/kg BD). Several days prior to the acute presentation, she developed severe abdominal pain. On admission to the medical ward, she presented with hypotension (90 systolic), pallor, cold peripheries, visible suprapubic bruising from enoxaparin injection sites, and palpable masses in the suprapubic region and left iliac fossa. Laboratory workup revealed acute hemoglobin drop to 67 g/L, elevated WBC (24.5 × 10⁹/L), and acute kidney injury. CT imaging of the abdomen and pelvis demonstrated left abdominal wall and pre-peritoneal hematoma collections with high attenuation on non-contrast imaging and contrast blush in two locations indicating active bleeding from branches of the left inferior epigastric and left lumbar arteries. A multidisciplinary team (interventional radiology, general surgery, hematology) elected conservative management given the patient's age, frailty, and comorbidities. She received 6 units of packed red blood cells over 5 days and tranexamic acid (1 g three times daily). No reversal agent or coagulation factors were administered as there was no coagulopathy and a significant interval had elapsed since the last enoxaparin injection. After 5 days of monitoring, hemoglobin normalized to 121 g/L, and she was discharged after 5 additional days without requirement for routine follow-up.
